scope: Combined DNS and non-DNS security validation records. A conservative count of recorded case/input executions, not unique scenarios or a fresh execution of every suite.

not_added_to_total.additional_config_unit_integration_cases: Covered by named tests; not added as an invented per-assertion total.
not_added_to_total.historical_builds_baseline_comparisons_a: Not accumulated across older evidence directories.
not_added_to_total.parser_assertions_and_concurrent_updates: Assertions and stress-loop operations are not counted as separate cases.

counting_notes: Each selected native report contributes its passing case entries once. Some reports exercise overlapping scenarios, including 151 structure cases repeated in the cumulative suite; this is an execution lower bound, not a deduplicated scenario inventory.
HTTP has 2618 shared fixtures exercised by both Go and Python; counted only once here.
Non-DNS randomized suites are counted once each, including only one of the fragment-pressure sanitizer runs.
Fuzz inputs can repeat; the recorded number is executions, not proof of unique payloads.
The 203-case interim DNS perimeter result was superseded by its 231-case completed suite, not added again.
No production deployment or universal attack-coverage claim follows from these counts.

The 2080-case exploratory protocol/encapsulation probe and 144-case exploratory mobility probe are included in the final 2224-case audit once; exploratory reruns and paired comparison runs are not added again.

The selected upstream DNS fuzz run is now 484788 executions from the stricter parser validation; it replaces the earlier 58484 execution selection. Historical client fuzz evidence remains tied to its original source hashes. Additional parser unit and cache-refresh checks are recorded separately, not added as per-assertion counts.

The 57 shared HTTP Range fixtures are counted once across Go/Python dispatch and diagnostic runs; baseline failures, repeated runs and the 18 additional direct-transport checks are not added again. These are admission controls, not additional Snort signatures.

The 129 shared Content-Range upload/response cases are counted once across Go/Python. The 79 baseline unexpected acceptances in each runtime, reruns, 10 direct-transport checks and six shared multipart header-budget checks are not added again. No new Snort SID was added.

The 308 shared conditional-header/validator fixtures are counted once across Go/Python. Baseline failures and repeated dispatch/diagnostic runs are excluded. The 29 additional direct-transport checks and 16 fixed-clock date checks are recorded separately rather than added to the execution lower bound.

The 194 shared response/request conditional correlation fixtures are counted once across Go and Python. The 89 baseline unexpected acceptances per runtime and all reruns are excluded. No new Snort SID was added.

The 123 shared complete JSON-response fixtures are counted once across Go and Python. The 63 baseline unexpected acceptances per runtime, existing UTF-8 denials and repeated runs are not added again. No new Snort SID was added.

The 88 shared HTTP request/response range-correlation cases are counted once across Go and Python. The 38 baseline unexpected acceptances per runtime and all reruns are excluded. Four existing Content-Range fixture request headers were corrected without adding cases; their older validation record is retained as historical. No new Snort SID was added.

The 129 shared multipart-content consistency cases are counted once across Go and Python. The 60 baseline unexpected acceptances per runtime and all reruns are excluded. Two large-overlap checks are recorded separately, not added to this lower bound. No new Snort SID was added.

The 291 shared address/resolver cases cover 254 address boundaries and 37 answer sets, counted once across Go and Python. Python had 18 baseline unexpected acceptances; Go already passed. Full-prefix checks for the 51 IANA assignments, baseline comparisons and reruns are not added to the case total. No Snort SID was added.

The four IPv4/IPv6 DNS transport-worker isolation cases are counted once. Their individual connection attempts, datagrams, before/after comparisons and race reruns are excluded. Controlled listeners and in-memory connections exercise source admission and worker lifecycle; this is not live flood or per-client fairness validation. No Snort SID was added.

The 17 controlled-time DNS cache lifetime and canceled-result cases are counted once. Eight cases failed before repair. Family/transport repetitions, boundary assertions, recovery calls and reruns are excluded. These are resolver-contract and cache-admission tests, not live network exploits. No Snort SID was added.

The 156 shared complete-range JSON cases are counted once across Go and Python. All 81 malformed complete documents were accepted at baseline. The additional 54-case Go MCP subset, baseline comparisons, reruns and two large-document checks are not added again. These checks operate on one bounded response and add no Snort SID.

The 20 Python inspection/transport deadline cases are counted once. Fourteen failed before repair. Seven named methods, baseline comparisons, assertions and full-suite reruns are not added again. One case uses a real local alarm; other expiry and boundary cases use controlled handler calls or clocks. No Snort SID was added.

The 20 Python DNS worker lifecycle cases are counted once. Nine failed before repair. Nine named methods, repeated requests/assertions within cases, baseline comparisons, existing deadline regressions and full-suite reruns are not added again. Two cases use real local alarms; all DNS lookups are simulated. No Snort SID was added.

The 190 shared HTTP Content-Disposition cases are counted once across Go and Python and parsed/final/interim checks. Both runtimes previously accepted 119 of the 120 rejected fixtures. Baseline comparisons, reruns, two MIME-context controls and the Unicode classification audit are excluded from this lower bound. The existing 114-case metadata corpus only adds a singleton declaration; its cases are unchanged. No Snort SID was added.

The 66 TLS service-identity cases (33 certificate variants under TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3) are counted once across Go and Python. Three Python native-capability startup checks are counted once separately. Go already passed; Python previously admitted ten denied certificate cases and lacked three runtime rejections. Baseline comparisons, repeated runs, public certificate/key files and individual assertions are not added. These are real local TLS exchanges with isolated fixture trust and simulated DNS, not external endpoint or deployment checks. No Snort SID was added.

XML admission adds 207 document fixtures, 112 media/framing/range fixtures and five maximum-body/early-budget checks, counted once across Go/Python and transport/MCP paths. The document corpus produces 619 transport checks per runtime and an additional 207 Go MCP checks; repeated layouts and baseline/rerun comparisons are not added again. The ASCII mutation audit contributes 25000 executions once across both runtimes, containing 23630 distinct payloads. Reproductions, preliminary audits, per-node/attribute/reference assertions and individual source files are not additional cases. Before repair, both runtimes forwarded all 146 document rejection fixtures; the original broker was not itself resolving external entities. No Snort SID was added.

The W3C XML TS 20130923 audit contributes 2001 applicable catalog input executions once across Go/Python, including 1974 required local-profile verdict checks and 27 optional-outcome parity checks. They contain 1983 distinct payloads. The 584 excluded edition/version cases and exploratory Python pass are not added.

Content-Digest contributes 130 final shared fixtures and seven selected capacity/metadata controls once across runtimes. The 127-case prototype baseline, revised capacity fixtures, additional complete-body assertions, overlapping Python controls and repeated runs are not accumulated. The 114 existing response-metadata cases are unchanged; their protected-name inventory now includes content-digest.

Request Content-Digest contributes 65 shared request fixtures and 23 selected direct-stream/cancellation/signature controls once across runtimes. The 34 baseline unexpected acceptances per path, diagnostic repetitions, three overlapping Python capacity controls, response corpus reruns and full regression reruns are excluded. No new Snort SID was added. The response digest validation record remains a historical snapshot preceding the shared-parser move.

Repr-Digest contributes 33 request fixtures, 63 response fixtures and four capacity/metadata controls once across languages and paths. The 17 request baseline unexpected acceptances per path, 30 response baseline unexpected acceptances per path, diagnostic/rerun executions and three overlapping Python capacity controls are excluded. Denials include explicit local-policy rejection of unavailable representation bytes. The existing 114 response metadata cases only change their protected-field inventory. No Snort SID is added.

Digest preferences contribute 108 request fixtures, 132 response fixtures and six metadata controls once across languages and paths. All 224 original baseline fixtures remain identical; sixteen bodyless response fixtures were added after repair. Baseline failures, runtime repetitions, diagnostic calls, repeated full runs and four overlapping Python metadata checks are excluded. Hints remain separate from actual integrity enforcement. No Snort SID is added.

The pinned HTTPWG Structured Fields audit contributes 1547 selected source cases (1536 distinct original field-value arrays), counted once across all four digest fields and Go/Python. Of these, 1543 have required profile verdicts and four permit either outcome and check parity. The 5324 field executions per runtime, 46 excluded cases, preliminary adapter-classification pass and selected regression reruns are not accumulated. No production parser change or Snort SID is added.

URI-reference metadata adds 133 request fixtures and 271 response fixtures plus six internal-field/MIME controls, counted once across Go/Python and all dispatch, diagnostic, interim, parsed and complete-body paths. All 404 fixtures are identical to baseline. Two direct request internal-list controls were added after repair. Baseline unexpected acceptances, runtime repetitions, preservation assertions and full-suite reruns are excluded. No new Snort SID or deployment is recorded.

TCP options add 844 selected native packet cases and 100000 deterministic randomized parser inputs once. All 844 packet inputs match baseline: 532 malformed cases were previously forwarded; the final regular and instrumented runs pass all 252 accepted controls and 592 denials. Initial plugin alignment diagnostics, baseline comparisons, preflights, 844 sanitizer repetitions, 2696 existing regression reruns, 1499749 fixed assertions and repeated parser builds are excluded. SID 9201017 adds one native blocking rule; no deployment is recorded.

TCP SACK permission adds 344 selected native conversations and 100000 deterministic randomized connection histories once. All 344 inputs and expectations match baseline: 184 unnegotiated admissions are now rejected, with all 152 wholly allowed controls and eight rejected-revocation controls preserved. Baseline/prototype/probe runs, 344 sanitizer repetitions, 3540 existing regression reruns, fixed assertions and repeated parser builds are excluded. SID 9201018 adds one production native blocking rule; fixture-only SID 9202999 is excluded. Evidence is local replay, not deployment.

The 3120 final TCP timestamp/SYN-data conversations are counted once. The matched baseline failed 684 cases (520 unexpected admissions and 164 false rejections); both final regular and instrumented runs pass. Baselines, prototype corpora, fixture corrections, probes, diagnostic builds, 3120 sanitizer repetitions, 3884 existing regression checks and a further 241-case artifact-metadata confirmation are excluded. Existing native events 129:4 and 129:14 enforce this cumulative engine repair; no Snort SID was added. Historical suite counts do not imply every suite was rerun against the newest engine.
